_readme: Quotes whose source text cannot be fetched by an automated request, so they cannot be
checked against a stored copy of the statute the way NJ's are (capitol.hawaii.gov returns
403 to curl and to WebFetch; only a real browser session gets the text).
Each entry was checked character-for-character against the enacted text in a real browser
on the date shown. `enactedTextSha256` is the SHA-256 of that page's text after curly
punctuation was normalized, bracketed struck-through material was removed so it reads as
ENACTED law, and whitespace was collapsed. Re-verifying means loading the source, applying
the same normalization, and confirming both the hash and the quote.
citation-fidelity.test.ts requires every quote in these statutes to appear here EXACTLY.
Editing a quote turns the suite red until someone re-reads the statute and updates this file.
That is the point: it makes re-verification the only way forward.
Exact procedure (fixed 2026-09-16, because the 2026-08-24 hash could not be reproduced from
its notes; the page's Last-Modified is Tue, 28 Apr 2026 18:37:11 GMT, so the text itself did
not change). In a real browser on the source page: clone document.body; remove every s,
strike, del, and inline-styled strikethrough element; take the clone's textContent; delete empty
bracket pairs with /\[\s*\]/g; then apply normalize() from citation-fidelity.test.tsx. SHA-256
of the UTF-8 result. On 2026-09-16 that text was 24,454 characters and all four quotes below

https://www.capitol.hawaii.gov/sessions/.label: HI HB 2021 CD1 (Act 259)
quotes: "High-speed electric device" means any device with a motor exceeding seven hundred fifty watts and capable of speeds over twenty-eight miles per hour.

An electric bicycle shall be required to be registered, and shall be subject to a permanent registration fee of $30, to be paid by the owners thereof to the director of finance. No person shall operate an electric bicycle on a public roadway, sidewalk, or bicycle facility unless it has been properly registered pursuant to this subsection. Failure to register may result in citation or temporary impoundment by a law enforcement officer or designated official pursuant to section 249-15.
No person under the age of sixteen shall operate a class 2 or class 3 electric bicycle unless under the direct supervision of a parent or guardian.
No person shall operate a high-speed electric device on a public roadway, a bicycle lane, a travel path, a bicycle facility, or other public area, such as a street, highway, or sidewalk.
